feedback.problem: Expressed in terms of ${log}_{4}$, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${4}^{x+1}={7}^{x}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{4}$ in both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{x+1} & ={7}^{x} \\ {log}_{4}⁡({4}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{4}⁡({4}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x}) \\ x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7) \\ x-x{log}_{4}⁡(7) & =-1 \\ x(1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)) & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$
